system.name: CLM
system.one_liner: a system that renders large 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes on a single consumer GPU by offloading Gaussians to CPU memory and loading them on demand, guided by frustum-culling sparsity and spatial locality

content.subject: why only Gaussians inside the camera's view frustum, clustered in one region, need to be accessed when rendering

elements.name: camera
elements.role: the viewpoint whose frustum determines which Gaussians are rendered

elements.name: frustum
elements.role: the camera's view volume, drawn as a pale-yellow 3D box, bounding which Gaussians can contribute to the rendered image

elements.name: in-frustum Gaussians
elements.role: four distinctly coloured ellipses (red, green, orange, cyan) inside the frustum, representing Gaussians that will be accessed when rendering this view

elements.name: out-of-frustum Gaussians
elements.role: numerous grey ellipses scattered through the rest of the scene, representing Gaussians that will not be accessed for this view

relations.what: the camera's sight lines define the frustum's shape
only Gaussians spatially located inside the frustum are coloured, i.e. considered accessed
Gaussians elsewhere in the scene, outside the frustum, are left grey/unaccessed

content.key_idea: Only the Gaussians that fall inside the camera's view frustum, a small, spatially clustered region of the whole scene, are accessed when rendering a view; everything outside the frustum can safely stay off the GPU.
content.reading_order: Start at the camera, follow its frustum lines outward into the pale-yellow box, compare the coloured Gaussians inside it against the grey Gaussians scattered through the rest of the scene.

summary: Figure 4 illustrates the frustum-culling sparsity that CLM exploits to decide which 3D Gaussians must be kept on the GPU. A camera view frustum is drawn as a pale-yellow box whose sides are traced by sight lines from the camera icon. Four example Gaussians, drawn as ellipses that fall inside this frustum, are coloured distinctly red, green, orange and cyan, representing Gaussians that will actually be accessed when rendering this view. Many more Gaussians are scattered throughout the rest of the scene bounding volume, shown as a dotted cube, but left grey, since they fall outside the frustum and are not touched for this render. The figure visually grounds two claims from the text: rendering a view only touches a sparse subset of the scene Gaussians, and that subset is spatially clustered rather than scattered, which is what makes offloading the rest to CPU memory practical.
summary_zh: 图4展示视锥剔除的稀疏性：相机视锥画成淡黄盒子，落在其中的4个高斯(椭圆)分别着红绿橙青色，表示渲染该视角时会被访问；场景其余(点线立方体内)大量高斯保持灰色、未被访问，说明渲染只需少量且空间聚集的高斯，其余可卸载到CPU内存。
